title: Intermediate
summary: Phrasal verbs for work, relationships and solving problems.

lessons.meaning: to stop trying, or to stop doing something
lessons.note: Separable: give up smoking / give it up. Also followed by -ing: give up smoking.
examples: Do not give up. You are almost there.
He gave up smoking last year.
She gave up her seat to an older man.
reallife: Encouraging someone: Keep going, do not give up!
Health: I gave up sugar to feel better.

mistakes.why: Give up is followed by -ing, not to + verb.

dialogue: A: This exercise is too hard. I want to give up.
B: Do not give up. Try one more time.
A: OK, you are right.
conversation.task: Say one thing you will never give up.

lessons.cloze: I was tired, but I did not ___.

options: stop trying
start again
give a present
assessment.why: Give up = stop trying.

options: He gave up smoking.
He gave up to smoke.
He gave up smoke.
assessment.why: Give up + -ing.

assessment.prompt: Please do not ___. You can do it! (give up)
assessment.why: Imperative: base form.

options: She gave it up.
She gave up it.
She up gave it.
assessment.why: A pronoun goes between give and up.

senses.meaning: to stop trying, or to stop doing something
senses.example: Do not give up. You are almost there.

lessons.meaning: to continue doing something

mistakes.why: Carry on is followed by -ing.

B: No problem. Please carry on.

stop
carry a bag

give up

assessment.why: Keep going = carry on.

senses.meaning: to continue doing something
senses.example: Please carry on. I am listening.

look behind
search for
